text:
zoe: Quick question: our ruby sampleapp CI started failing on the packaging step when consumers try `rake build` inside sampleapp. Error: `gemspec not found` even though gemspec exists in ../ruby-sdk. This only happens in the packaged tarball CI job (integration smoke). Anyone seen this packaging mismatch between local path gem and published gem?

liam: Likely because the sampleapp uses a path gem in Gemfile: `gem 'redwood', path: '../ruby-sdk'`. When we run `rake build` inside the sampleapp tar, the relative path no longer points to the SDK since the tarball layout flattens or strips parent dir.

zoe: Ah true. Locally devs clone monorepo and `bundle install` resolves the path. CI runs build inside the sampleapp archive and can't reference outside.

devrel_alejandra: Two straightforward fixes: 1) change sampleapp Gemfile to prefer a released gem as fallback (try local path, else `gem 'redwood'`), 2) add a small prepack step that vendors a built gem into the tarball (`vendor/redwood.gem`) so CI and downstream users without the monorepo can run it. Which feels less surprising for newcomers?

liam: Fallback gem is friendlier for quickstart users. Prepack vendor is better for internal CI that needs deterministic code. We can do both: fallback for public quickstart tarballs + vendor for our CI packaging job.

zoe: I can open a PR. Plan: modify Gemfile to `begin; gem 'redwood', path: '../ruby-sdk'; rescue LoadError; gem 'redwood'; end` — although bundler's DSL doesn't support rescue that way. Better: use `if File.exist?(File.expand_path('../ruby-sdk', __dir__)); gem 'redwood', path: '../ruby-sdk' else gem 'redwood' end`

liam: Also add `Rakefile` prepack task: `task :prepack do sh 'gem build ../ruby-sdk/redwood.gemspec && mkdir -p vendor && mv redwood-*.gem vendor/' end` and wire into packaging CI step. Add note in README explaining monorepo vs packaged use.

devrel_alejandra: Sounds good. Please include a small CI job matrix change so the tarball build runs the prepack task before zipping. And add a test that `bundle exec ruby -e "require 'redwood'"` succeeds in a clean environment inside the tarball. That should catch regressions.

zoe: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapps/pull/128 - includes Gemfile fallback, prepack Rake task, README note, and CI tweak.

release-bot: Release checklist triggered for PR #128. Ensure changelog entry and one approving review.

ci-bot: CI: pipeline started for branch "fix/sampleapp-prepack". packaging job queued.

liam: Small follow-up: we should avoid long/complex Ruby code inside Gemfile; some bundler versions error on `File.expand_path` in certain environments. Keep the check tiny and comment intention. Also add a comment pointing to docs on contributing with monorepo.

zoe: Good point. I'll add an inline comment and a link to CONTRIBUTING.md about running sampleapps in-mono. Also added a tiny `bin/install-local` script that builds the gem and runs `bundle config set --local path 'vendor/bundle' && bundle install` for devs on Windows.

ci-bot: packaging job passed. lint and unit jobs passed. :white_check_mark:

devrel_alejandra: Merging after one more approval. Thanks for catching this, Zoe — should cut down confusion for folks downloading quickstarts and not using the monorepo.

zoe: Awesome. Will follow up with a short note in #general for community users who reported this earlier.
